channel.title: Sunday
channel.description: Notes on AI engineering, projects, and small tools by Sunday.

item.title: Transformers, Explained by Training One
item.description: Every piece of a GPT-style transformer, from the tokenizer to attention to sampling, built from scratch in PyTorch, trained on 557 million tokens of children's stories in half an hour on one gaming GPU, and running live in your browser.

item.title: SAM 3: Segment Anything by Name, and What It Does for Your Labeling
item.description: How SAM 3 turns a noun phrase or one example box into every matching object in an image, how its detector is built, and a measured experiment: auto-labeling a real detection dataset with SAM 3 and training YOLO26 on the result.

item.title: DINOv3: Learning to See Without Labels, and Using It in Practice
item.description: How DINOv3 learns general-purpose image features from 1.7 billion unlabeled images, what those features look like, the main ways to use a frozen DINOv3 backbone, and a measured deep dive into memory-bank defect detection on MVTec AD.

item.title: Vision Transformers, Built from Scratch
item.description: How a transformer reads an image: patches, tokens, positions, attention and registers. Build a modern ViT in PyTorch, load the released DINOv3 weights into it unchanged, and look at what it computes.

item.title: RT-DETR and YOLO26: Two Roads to NMS-Free Detection
item.description: How two real-time detectors got rid of non-maximum suppression: a transformer that predicts a set, and a CNN trained to answer once. The full pipeline, verified PyTorch code, real model outputs and a side-by-side comparison.

item.title: ResNet, Explained from Scratch
item.description: Why a 56-layer network can train worse than a 20-layer one, how residual connections fix it, and a PyTorch implementation that matches torchvision weight for weight.

item.title: Word Motions in Vim
item.description: The handful of word motions that make moving through code feel fast.

item.title: Markdown Cheatsheet
item.description: Every Markdown feature and frontmatter field this blog supports, in one place.
